goal.title: Find a planet around two suns
goal.plain: The whole project in one line. We search NASA's TESS light for a planet that circles two stars at once. Finding one is a win, and so is proving, with measured numbers, that none was there to find.
goal.tree: Find a circumbinary planet in TESS data, or prove a clean, measured null. Both are wins (29 Oct 2026).

nodes.title: The eclipse mask hides the transit

nodes.title: Blind spot for fast binaries
nodes.id_tree: Blind spot: binaries of 5 to 10 days
nodes.plain: Binaries that orbit each other in 5 to 10 days are noisier, and the tool finds very few test planets around them.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: A feared gap in our bad-data filter for newer QLP light curves does not exist: every flagged moment is already removed.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: Measured fairly (per hour of searched light), the extra real dips near momentum dumps are not a clear excess, and the second star list does not repeat the pattern.
leaves.why: It weakens the idea that the dump-shape rule's extra events are simply dump artefacts, so Fable must design that rule without leaning on timing alone.
leaves.explanation: Codex counted real and upside-down events by how far they sit from a dump, divided by how many hours of light were searched there, and checked the first star list's pattern on the second. Claude's quick count found more near-dump real events on the first list; Codex's full rerun is the faithful one, and the 15-event gap is being traced.
leaves.technical: G2 contains-a-dump 25/5, E +0.157 per 1,000 h (95% -0.046 to +0.301); G3 7/3, -0.016. Two keys: G3 68/26 equal; G2 flip 62 equal; G2 real 166 (Claude) vs 151 (Codex).

leaves.label: LIKELY
leaves.plain: TESS's own 2-second pointing record shows the telescope shakes hard at each momentum dump but stays calm before it, so the shaking does not explain the extra fake-looking dips we see hours before dumps.
leaves.why: It saves a 46 GB download and tells Fable the pre-dump excess needs another explanation.
leaves.explanation: Our light curves smooth out fast shaking, so we read the spacecraft's pointing directly for one sector. The fast shake jumps 4.5 times at the dump and stays a little high for hours after. Before the dump the pointing only drifts slowly by a tiny amount.
leaves.technical: Sector 11, 4 cameras, 15 dumps. 30-min RMS ratio: 0.95 at 12 to 6 h before, up to 1.06 in the last hour, 4.5 at the dump, 1.13 to 1.28 after. Slow drift 0.3 to 0.6 arcsec (about 0.02 to 0.03 pixel), smooth. One sector only (UNCERTAIN for other eras).

leaves.label: CONFIRMED

leaves.explanation: Planets around fast binaries cross their stars quickly, so their dips are short. The same short box also picks up eclipse leftovers and spacecraft artefacts.

leaves.plain: A run now takes its star set and options from its own settings file, and stops loudly if any input is missing.
leaves.why: A leftover shell setting or an empty data folder could otherwise send the one-shot G1 run to the wrong stars without anyone noticing.
leaves.explanation: The old runner read two shell variables and wrote "missing" into its fingerprint when a file was absent. The new helper refuses both cases before any light is read.
leaves.technical: apply() sets SS_SET and VESPER_OPTS from JSON and refuses conflicting shell values; require() checks data folder, manifest, best-product table, targets and at least one light-curve file per star. 8 of 8 tests pass; mutations of the conflict and file checks go red. Not in the frozen hash list. G1 runner imports it.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: The wobble of the star's light centre in our own files cannot tell the telescope's fake dips near momentum dumps from real planets.
leaves.why: It rules out a cheap safety check for the dump-shape rule; the only independent check left needs TESS's 2-second pointing records.
leaves.explanation: The fake dips come from fast pointing jitter. Our light curves average the light centre over 2 to 30 minutes, which smooths that jitter away. Events the shape rule would free wobble no more than planted planets do.
leaves.technical: Method and pass written first. G2: 25 freed real events against 415 planted crossings in the dump zone, Mann-Whitney p 0.53 (needed under 0.01); a guard at the planets' 90th percentile (J 1.90) holds 4 of 25. G3: 3 events, holds 1 (needs 2). Exploratory drift measure: weak hint (p 0.05). First run had a sector-name lookup bug (s2019), fixed before reading results.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: TESS's pointing wobbles more and more before each momentum dump, spilling starlight out of the aperture: a fake dip that our upside-down check can never see. A version of the dump-shape rule that only relaxes after the dump is fair but gains only 4 planets, so it is not the route to 0.50.
leaves.why: explains the blind spot Codex found, and moves Fable's attention to the eclipse-timing fix, the bigger lever.
leaves.explanation: Four papers agree: scatter grows for about a day before a dump (Vanderburg 2019), pointing stays disturbed for hours after (Eisner 2019), with ramps within half a day (Wong 2020), and dumps mimic transits (Guerrero 2021). The planet gains of the shape rule sit in the same place as its fake dips, so only a direct wobble measure could separate them.
ids: DSp (dump-shape relief only after the dump)

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: Codex tried to measure each binary's true eclipse times from TESS itself; its own checks failed, mostly because the method sometimes mistakes a binary with two equal eclipses for one with half the period.
leaves.why: the eclipse-mask fix (the biggest fixable planet loss) needs these times; the problem is now narrow and nameable, so Fable's Monday round can fix it.
leaves.explanation: On control stars whose timing we trust, 13 of 58 fits landed on half the true period and none of those agreed; on the correct period, 38 of 45 agreed within about a minute and a half (0.001 d). The eclipses that the narrower mask let through do line up with Codex's flagged tracks (18 of 21), which supports the earlier finding that the catalogue's times are wrong for those stars.
leaves.technical: control agreement 28/60 periods, 31/60 epochs (54 needed); injection robust on all 9 testable stars (max shift 0.039 widths), 11 untestable. Fence check: frozen files 0, fence ids 0; branch not merged.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED

On the bench it frees 1 planet but 5 upside-down events, and the upside-down background rises. Switching the opposite-sign flag off entirely adds 3 upside-down alarms with no planet gained.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: Flagging NASA's known spacecraft trouble moments passes our rule: it costs almost nothing and removes 4 false alarms. Combined with the dump-shape rule, it lifts planet recovery to 49.98% with no more upside-down alarms, just under the 50% line G1 needs.
leaves.why: the first combination that gains planets without more upside-down alarms; it goes to Fable's round on Monday and Codex's second key.
leaves.explanation: On its own, the known-events flag loses 2 planets out of about 1,100 and removes 4 upside-down and 2 real false alarms. The dump-shape rule alone adds 20 planets but also 4 upside-down alarms; the known-events flag cancels exactly those. Caution: the real-light alarms rise by 28, and the upside-down meter is partly blind near dumps, so the real cost may be higher than it looks.
leaves.technical: P (equal weight) OAE 0.4828, OAEk 0.4811, OAED 0.5016, OAEkD 0.4998; tier-1 background real/upside-down 176/83, 174/79, 207/87, 204/83; paired control passes in all 5 bins for all four. Rules written before the run.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: Two of our statistics tools told small untruths; both are fixed and tested before G1 uses them.
leaves.why: G1's verdict will be printed by these tools, so they must say exactly what was tested and what a null can and cannot rule out.
leaves.explanation: The gate tool said PASS for the slow-binary bins even when no test dips had been planted there; it now says "PASS ON TESTED BINS (3 of 5)". The readout's "power" line used a simpler test than the real verdict and called its result an exclusion; it now runs the real rule on simulated strong signals and calls the result a sensitivity.
leaves.technical: gate_judge: PASS, FAIL, PASS ON TESTED BINS, INCOMPLETE; rerun on sealed G3 rows: numbers identical. s1_sensitivity: 8 filed chances reproduced; crossings G3 55 and 60 added, G2 60 and 70 (equal to Codex 002); mutation red. Filed results unchanged.
ids: FIX 86 (the readout's power line used the wrong test)
FIX 87 (gates said PASS on untested period bins)

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: We now have a list of 19 known moments when the telescope itself misbehaved, taken from NASA's sector notes; flagging them would remove a few false alarms at almost no cost.
leaves.why: a cheap, low-risk fix for the sector 4 kind of false alarm, ready for the next fix round.
leaves.explanation: Most events at those moments are already held by our flags; only 6 reached the top tier. The flag would touch 33 of 5,308 planted planet crossings.
leaves.technical: 2 real and 4 upside-down tier-1 background events removed; planet-level cost not yet measured.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: Finding spacecraft glitches from our own data alone does not work: it would also flag about a quarter of real planet transits.
leaves.why: the sector 4 type of false alarm needs a short list of known spacecraft events from TESS's own notes instead.
leaves.explanation: With hundreds of stars, ordinary events line up by chance all the time, so "many stars at once" is not a clean signal across cameras.
leaves.technical: K=3 other stars, any camera, 0.1 d: background 22 real / 15 upside-down, planted crossings 1,291 of 5,308 at risk.

leaves.plain: Book 2.11.7: the home recap now tells the evening's eclipse-mask result and the next step.
leaves.why: the daily recap rule.
leaves.explanation: Recap only; no other page changed.
leaves.technical: footer and versions row bumped.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: Letting a planet's look-alike second transit off the "dominated" rule catches 2 more test planets but adds 7 upside-down false alarms, so it is rejected.
leaves.why: keeps OAE as it is for Petrova 1.1; the twin-transit side effect stays a known small cost.
leaves.explanation: Noise also comes in look-alike pairs, so the exemption frees false events too.
leaves.technical: OAE 527 dips, P 48.28%, background 176/83; OAEt 529, 48.46%, 182/90; paired control passes for both.
ids: OAE (fairness fix for the dominated rule)

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: About a third of our top-tier events on real light are deeper than any planet could make; they are almost surely eclipses.
leaves.why: a guard that drops them would cut false work in G1, but our test bench cannot yet show it never drops a planet.
leaves.explanation: 51 of 176 real and 16 of 83 upside-down top-tier events are over 3% deep. The bench's planted planets stop at 0.6% deep, so it cannot price the guard. Better than a fixed number: a ceiling per star from its size.
leaves.technical: thresholds 10k/20k/30k/50k ppm: real 75/56/51/39, upside-down 35/19/16/7; on V2's 38 new real events only 7 over 30k.
ids: FIX 96 (events deeper than any planet reach tier 1)
Codex 011 (the mask-timing test with the fairness fix on)

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: A known jump in the telescope's pointing in sector 4 makes fake dips and bumps on many stars at once; our filter catches most but not all.
leaves.why: each one that slips through is a false alarm in G1.
leaves.explanation: At TJD 1413.26 TESS loaded the right guide star table and its pointing shifted about 4 arcseconds. 50 of our sector 4 events straddle that moment; 3 reached tier 1 because only two stars per camera shared the moment, under the 3-star rule.
leaves.technical: fix idea: a known-spacecraft-events list from the data release notes, flagged like a momentum dump for both arms; to be measured on T156 and the background meters.

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: The narrower eclipse masks fail: they stay just under 50% and add a few false alarms, because the wide padding was hiding eclipses whose catalogue times are wrong.
leaves.why: the fix for FIX 94 must measure where each binary's eclipses really are in TESS, period included, before narrowing anything.
leaves.explanation: With the fairness fix on, both variants catch about 16 more planets (P about 49.6%). About half the extra events on real light are deep eclipses (up to 17% deep). One binary repeats a 10,000 ppm eclipse every 31.81 days; its catalogue says 30.98.
leaves.technical: V0/V1/V2 + OAE: P 48.20 / 49.61 / 49.66%; all-design background 176/83, 209/86, 205/89; T156 dips 500, 524, 523; paired control passes every bin. 18 of 38 new V2 real events are 8,000 ppm+ or SNR 50+, on 10 stars.
ids: RS-027 (root cause of the new events)
TIC 140760434 (the binary whose catalogue period was off by 0.84 days)

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: The fairness fix lets two more real TOI-1338 b transits through (6 of 13 instead of 4), but it can let a planet's stronger transit hide its weaker one.
leaves.why: the fix helps a real planet, not only planted ones; its one side effect is now explained.
leaves.explanation: Sectors 89 and 93 were held because a rival event was as strong; under OAE eclipse-labelled rivals no longer count. TIC 172900988 b has two transits 4.95 d apart; OAE counts the stronger one as a rival of the weaker. No effect today (both held by edge flags), but it matters once those are fixed.
leaves.technical: identity 10 of 10; single-transit tier-1 31% to 46%; mask timing change cannot touch TOI-1338 (term at most 0.005 d). Refinement idea (NOT TESTED): ignore a same-sign rival matching depth and duration.
ids: OAE (fairness fix for the dominated rule)
RS-025 Q5 (known planets under the new rules)
TOI-1338 b (a known planet that orbits two suns)
TIC 172900988 b (a known two-sun planet with two transits close together)

leaves.plain: Codex re-tests the narrower eclipse mask with our fairness fix switched on, against a pass rule written before the results.
leaves.why: it decides whether the biggest known gain (+25 planets, past the 50% bar) can be adopted for G1.
leaves.explanation: 010 ran without OAE, so its fairness failures were inherited. 011 also finds out where the 30 or so new events on real light come from: eclipse leftovers or something else.
leaves.technical: pass = P 50%+, paired control passes every bin, upside-down background not higher than V0+OAE, T156 more planets with no more upside-down alarms.
ids: Codex 011 (mask timing with the OAE fix)
OAE (fairness fix for the dominated rule)

leaves.plain: Before Codex 011 reports, the rule for what we do with its result is written down.
leaves.why: the decision cannot be bent to fit the numbers afterwards.
leaves.explanation: V2 already gets 23 of the 25 possible planets, so the full eclipse-time fit can add at most about 2. If V2 passes, adopt V2; if it fails only on upside-down alarms near eclipses, build the full fit; if the new events sit far from eclipses, stop and research; if both pass, V2 over V1.
leaves.technical: 23/25 = 92% of the upper bound; V2 vs V1 upside-down 8 vs 5 is within counting error.

leaves.plain: Fable's Monday brief is ready: three real tasks with a work log each, then it writes its working method as a skill for Opus.
leaves.why: keeps Fable's way of working after access ends.
leaves.explanation: Tasks: design the FIX 94 mask timing fix, judge what goes into Petrova 1.1, plan the shortest safe path to G1. A held-out design task (the step flag) tests the skill on Opus afterwards; Fable is told not to open it.
leaves.technical: finish by Mon 23:00 Kuwait; meters read before and after each task.
ids: Fable (the strongest model, access ends Tue 17 Nov 01:00 Kuwait)

leaves.plain: Star ids and star data may appear plainly in the book and on the Tree; they are no longer treated as private.
leaves.why: the Tree can now show real stars and events instead of counts only.
leaves.explanation: Ahmed: the book is his own notebook and nobody knows the link. Science rules stay: sealed runs stay blind until the preregistered analysis, fence A and B stars are never searched, outward actions (emails, CTOI, ExoFOP, posts) need his yes. Leads show at once, marked 'not checked yet'.
leaves.technical: the publish script's privacy scan has to be loosened to match before the first star id is published (part of T160).

leaves.plain: Every finished piece of work becomes one small drop file; a script turns the drops into the Tree, the book and the bookkeeping, and publishes.
leaves.why: today each task needs about six hand edits; with drops it needs one file, so the Tree stays current without being a burden.
leaves.explanation: Ahmed's idea. Drops start now; the builder is built after G1 as part of T160. Python sorts, checks and formats; it never writes the words.
leaves.technical: plan section 9; drops are Markdown with a small header (type, node, date, label, status, links, ids, supersedes).
ids: T160 (the Tree build, first after G1)

leaves.label: CONFIRMED
leaves.plain: Narrowing the eclipse mask's timing padding catches about 25 more test planets and lifts the score past the 50% bar, but lets more noise through on the stars it affects.
leaves.why: it is the biggest single fixable loss we know, and the first change that crosses the G1 bar on its own.
leaves.explanation: The mask hides eclipses with a window widened by how unsure the eclipse timing is. On 112 G2 stars with old timings that padding is so wide it blanks whole light curves. Turning the padding off (V1) or recentring the windows on the real eclipses with a cap (V2) gives the planets back, but the same stars then show more events on real light and a few more upside-down alarms.
leaves.technical: P (equal-bin dip recovery, 1,098 planets) V0 48.37% (528), V1 50.68% (553), V2 50.54% (551); bumps 486, 501, 503. Affected-star background real/upside-down V0 61/3, V1 95/5, V2 90/8. Paired dip-vs-bump 99% intervals fail in 20 to 27.4 d and 27.4+ d for all three, including V0, so that failure is the pre-OAE baseline, not the variants. Eclipse-overlap proxy: no new real-event centres inside eclipse windows (approximate for missing secondaries). RS-025 cause counts reproduced exactly (690 found, 408 not). Not adoptable yet: re-run with OAE on, and explain the 29 to 34 new real-light events.
ids: FIX 94 (mask timing padding blanks light curves)
RS-025 (flag prices and the 408 missed planets)

leaves.plain: Research: TESS-era eclipse times; timing bug is G2 only (110 of 420 stars, 706 of 711 blanked curves); Oddo et al.
leaves.technical: TESS-era eclipse times; timing bug is G2 only (110 of 420 stars, 706 of 711 blanked curves); Oddo et al. 2026 recentre per sector; FIX 94 design draft for Fable. research/stage3/rs026/EPHEMERIS-AND-FILTER-RESEARCH-2026-11-14.md

leaves.technical: the broken-light-curve guards nd and dg change nothing under B (P 48.11%, background 174/79 unchanged; 61 unphysical design events already ignored by OAE). Safe physics guards, no gain. research/stage3/rs032/ND-DG-RULE-2026-11-14.md.

leaves.plain: Build: it holds 57% of real and 51% of upside-down tier-1 background and 59 of the 95 real excess, but holding it costs 40 planets (P 48.1% to 44.6%, fast binaries) and fails the paired control in one bin.

phases.title: Learning the sky and the first tools
phases.plain: The project starts. What is known, where the gap is, our first light curves and our first planet-finding tool, Vesper.

phases.title: The first sealed searches
phases.plain: G2 and G3, searches run once under rules written in advance. Both found no planet, and both taught us where the tool was weak.

phases.title: The audit and Petrova
phases.plain: An outside audit found the eclipse mask could hide planets. The tool was rebuilt and frozen as Petrova, then searched the old lists again.

phases.title: The bench and the fix rounds
phases.plain: Codex joins. Every proposed fix is measured on 2,000 planted planets, with fake ones counted too, before it may enter the tool.

phases.title: Learning first
phases.plain: The hunt pauses so you can learn everything it rests on. The Tree and a new textbook are built.
